feat(agents): bring existing Codex and Claude sessions into ptyd

#11·2018kguo·feat/import-agent-sessions

Codex and Claude conversations started in other tabs now show up in ptyd status --discover, and Enter opens a ptyd terminal on the same running worker. The native daemons stay the owners. ptyd only launches their own client after a fresh listing confirms the conversation, both before and after the launch.

Adds github.com/coder/websocket to talk to the Codex daemon over its Unix socket.

How a running Codex or Claude conversation reaches a ptyd terminal

1A launch is decided from native state alone

native.Plan turns one observed session into the argv of the agent's own client. Nothing from the HTTP request reaches the command line except the conversation id, which must be a full UUID.

  • session.go internal/native/ part+48
1
The trust boundary Command, directory and Claude job id come from a fresh native observation, never from the request. POST /terminals can already run any command, so what this protects is narrower: a terminal that carries a Source was built from what the native daemon reported.
2
Resume is opt-in A stopped Claude conversation is listed but refuses import without --resume, because resuming starts a new worker and a model request. Decide whether the picker should offer that in one keypress or keep the flag.

2Discovery fails closed

Both providers are probed in parallel through their own CLIs or daemon socket. Anything incomplete or ambiguous becomes an issue or an Unavailable row, never a guess.

  • discover.go internal/native/ part+52
  • codex.go internal/native/ part+25
3
Handoff duplicates block import During /bg, Claude briefly reports a foreground and a background worker for one conversation. Both rows become Unavailable instead of picking the newer one, so a user who refreshes too early sees a disabled row.
Only these lines are in review →
4
Check: Codex PID is the daemon For Codex, WorkerPID is the peer of the daemon socket, shared by every thread. The identity check in import therefore proves the daemon did not restart, not that this thread is still the one loaded.
Only these lines are in review →

3Import checks the worker before and after the launch

ImportAgent looks the conversation up, launches the frontend, then looks it up again. If the worker, directory or process identity moved in between, the new frontend is closed and the import is declined.

  • import.go internal/terminal/ part+84
5
No reuse of imported windows A running imported window for the same conversation is refused rather than reused. Its Source is where it was launched from, and the user may have switched conversations inside it since.
6
The second lookup The frontend has already been spawned when this check runs. On a mismatch it is closed at line 126, so confirm that closing a codex resume --remote or claude attach client never stops the worker it was attached to.
Only these lines are in review →

4Imported terminals do not outlive their viewers

An imported terminal is a view, so it closes when the last viewer detaches or when nobody claims it within a minute. Restart and restore refuse it and ask for a fresh import.

  • attach.go internal/terminal/ part+41
  • restore.go internal/terminal/+3
  • types.go internal/terminal/ part+2
7
Detach closes the frontend When the last viewer detaches, the imported terminal closes and the native worker keeps running. A late attach to that id gets an error and has to import again, which is the price of never reusing a stale frontend.
2 more hunks of this file are not in review →
8
Imports do not survive a daemon restart After ptyd restarts, imported terminals stay as ghosts and cannot be restored in place. Users re-import from the picker, which re-runs every check above.
